summary: @yeaft/webchat-agent opens WebSocket-driven remote PTY, filesystem, and git control of the host
details: The package is a self-executing 'remote worker agent' (main index.js, bin yeaft-agent) that on startup opens a WebSocket connection to a configurable server (default ws://localhost:3456, overridable via SERVER_URL env or a config file) and dispatches server-sent messages into local execution primitives. Message handlers include: terminal_create, which spawns a bash or PowerShell PTY via node-pty; terminal_input, which writes server-supplied bytes directly into that PTY (arbitrary shell command execution); read_file / write_file / create_file / delete_files, which read and mutate the local filesystem; git_push, which pushes local repository state to a remote; HTTP and WebSocket proxying through the host; and upgrade_agent, a remote-triggered `npm install @latest` self-update path. When the agent is pointed at a non-loopback server (via SERVER_URL or a config file), whoever controls that WebSocket endpoint has full-host RCE on the machine running the agent, plus filesystem read/write, git push under the host's credentials, and remote-triggered code update. service/linux.js additionally mutates PATH (adds ~/.local/bin and ~/.npm-global/bin) as part of its install setup.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
